name: Seraiah
overview: Seraiah was a male figure known primarily as the secretary to King David, serving in an official capacity during David's reign. Scripture identifies him by this unique role, highlighting his involvement in the administrative affairs of the kingdom. Beyond this, no additional personal or tribal details are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Seraiah carries meanings related to the Lord, such as 'YHWH persists,' 'YHWH is prince,' and 'YHWH contends,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. He is also referred to by the title 'secretary,' denoting a learned writer or scribe responsible for record-keeping. Additionally, the name Shavsha appears as an alternative proper name associated with this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Seraiah beyond his role as secretary to David. There are no known relatives or descendants mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Seraiah's significance lies in his administrative service to King David, illustrating the organized governance under David's rule. As secretary, he contributed to the management and documentation of royal affairs, a role that underscores the importance of faithful stewardship in God's appointed leadership. His presence in Scripture, though brief, reflects the functioning of the Davidic kingdom and its reliance on trusted officials.
